question.ask: How many products are out of stock?
question.whyItMatters: Esme reorders everything marked Out first.

text.text: On hand fills in for you: opening stock plus what you received, minus what you sold. Stock level turns to Reorder soon at the reorder point and to Out at zero, so there is nothing to update by hand.
Match the delivery to the purchase order
Mark the order Received and set the date
Note any shortage with the supplier
Reorder when stock reaches the reorder point.
Order enough to cover the supplier lead time plus two weeks.
Never let a best seller show Out for more than a day.
Quantities received and sold come from orders, so mark orders Received and Delivered promptly.
How the stock level is decided

Each product carries three numbers: opening stock, a reorder point and what has moved since. When on hand falls to the reorder point the product shows Reorder soon; at zero or below it shows Out. A negative figure means a sale was recorded before the delivery was marked Received, which is the first thing to check.
Multiply the units you sell per week by the supplier lead time in weeks, then add a cushion for a slow delivery. Review the number every quarter, because seasons change how fast things sell.
Count what is on the shelf and compare it with the numbers in each product.
Fix any differences with a note
Reset stock status for every product

If the shelf count differs from On hand, do not overwrite anything. Find the missing receipt or sale, enter it, and the figure corrects itself. If nothing explains the gap, change Opening stock by the difference and write the reason in the product notes.
